panels.title: AI error ratio (non-2xx, 5m)
panels.description: Shows 0 when traffic is healthy; No data only when there is no AI traffic at all.

panels.title: Active SSE streams
panels.description: Streams open at the scrape instant (10s sampling). Short streams that start and finish between scrapes are not visible here - 0 is normal when the backend completes streams quickly; see the requests/s panels for volume and the trend panel for history.

panels.title: KV subscribers up
panels.description: KV-cache routing health: min(loxilb_kv_subscriber_connected) across prefill EPs (1=all connected, 0=any rebuilding). Absent until a KV-exact deployment registers its first subscriber.

panels.title: AI requests/s by model
panels.description: Counter increments at SSE stream COMPLETION — long streams appear only when they finish.

panels.title: AI requests/s by status
panels.description: Real backend status codes (post-audit).

panels.title: Request duration p95 by model
panels.description: Buckets reach 300 s for SSE streams.

panels.title: Request duration distribution (p50/p90/p99)
panels.description: Latency spread from loxilb_ai_request_duration_seconds histogram. (Replaces the classic-histogram heatmap, which does not render reliably in Grafana 11.)

panels.title: Active SSE streams (trend)
panels.description: History of the instantaneous gauge (10s samples). Sub-second streams rarely overlap a scrape.

panels.title: Tier-1.5 hits vs spills vs fallthrough/s
panels.description: Aggregate comparison of tier-1.5 routing outcomes. hits/spills are summed across endpoints here (the underlying counters carry ep_idx); see 'Tier-1.5 hits by endpoint' for the per-endpoint split.

panels.title: Tier-1.5 hits by endpoint
panels.description: Per-endpoint KV cache-hit routing decisions (ep_idx = endpoint index in the LB rule). Shows how tier-1.5 exact-match routing distributes prompts across the pool - distinct prompt prefixes should pin to distinct endpoints.

panels.title: Rate-limit hits/s
panels.description: Denied requests are NOT counted in loxilb_ai_requests_total — this is the only place throttling is visible. Requires an AI API key carrying rate_limit_rps (POST /config/ai/apikey); 'No data' without keyed quota configured.

panels.title: Model-not-allowed/s
panels.description: Requires an AI API key with an allowed_models list (POST /config/ai/apikey); the request must carry that key so llb_ai_validate_key can reject a disallowed model. 'No data' without keyed allow-list. NOTE: the apikey REST endpoint is unimplemented on some images (returns 422/'not yet implemented').

panels.title: Token quota (TPM) — needs API-key security with per-tenant token limits
panels.description: Empty unless the AI gateway runs with the user service and a tenant carries a tokens-per-minute limit. The series are fed by the quota consume path, and utilisation/headroom are computed at scrape time from live limiter state.

panels.title: Tokens/s by kind
panels.description: Tokens metered against completed responses, split prompt vs completion. Charged at the quota-consume call, so a stream contributes when it completes.

panels.title: Tokens/s by model
panels.description: Same charges as the panel on the left, split by model. Use with the per-model quota panel below to see which model is spending a tenant's budget.

panels.title: Tenant quota utilisation
panels.description: Fraction of the per-tenant tokens-per-minute quota spent and not yet refilled, computed at scrape time. Can exceed 100%: a charge settled after admission puts the bucket in debt, which then decays as it refills.

panels.title: Per-model quota utilisation
panels.description: Same measure keyed tenant+model. A tenant can sit well under its aggregate quota while one model is already latched — this is the panel that shows it.

panels.title: Quota denials/s by tenant
panels.description: Requests refused at the gate because the tenant's token quota was exhausted. Denials with utilisation below 100% mean the deny came from the deep-debt path, not the reservation check.

panels.title: Estimate-net charges vs missing usage
panels.description: Left series counts TOKENS charged from the estimate net (no usage object in the response); right series counts RESPONSES that had no readable usage. Different units on purpose — a rising ratio between them means responses are getting more expensive to guess at.

panels.title: Quota headroom by tenant
panels.description: limit x (1 - utilisation): tokens the tenant may still spend in the current window. Goes negative while the bucket is in post-hoc debt.

panels.title: Cold fail-open windows
panels.description: Times this node began serving quota-limited traffic with empty in-memory quota state and no peer warm-up, over the dashboard range. Non-zero means a window was under-enforced after a restart.

panels.title: L7 byte shaper (Tier-1 QoS) — only on fullproxy rules with a policer attached
panels.description: Empty until a policer is attached to a fullproxy rule. Only a direction the policy actually shapes is exported, so a missing series means that direction is not shaped rather than idle; a service that stops being shaped stops being exported entirely.

panels.title: Shaped throughput by service and direction
panels.description: Payload bytes the Tier-1 shaper granted, per shaped service and direction, with the configured CIR as a dashed reference. These are PLAINTEXT payload bytes measured inside the relay — never comparable with the eBPF policer's L3 wire-byte counters.

panels.title: Bucket saturation (delayed / passed)
panels.description: Share of granted bytes that had to wait through at least one park. This is a SATURATION signal, not a throttled fraction: once the bucket is empty essentially every read follows a park, so a service pinned at its CIR sits near 100%. Use parks/s and mean park below to size the delay.

panels.title: Parks/s
panels.description: Rate at which the shaper parked a reader because its bucket was empty. Rises with offered load above the CIR; zero while a shaped service stays under its rate.

panels.title: Mean park duration
panels.description: park_seconds / parks over the interval — how long a throttled reader waits per park. Parks that never resumed (connection torn down while throttled) are not counted, so this measures served delay.

panels.title: Readers parked now
panels.description: Connections the shaper is holding at this instant (bucket park-ring depth). A ring that stays near its 256-entry cap means throttled connections are queueing faster than refills release them.

panels.title: Bucket level vs burst depth
panels.description: Tokens available in the bucket against its burst depth. A level sitting at zero means the service is rate-bound; a level pinned at the burst depth means the shaper is configured but idle.

panels.title: KV attestation
panels.description: Attestation ladder state per strict rule, enforcement faults, probe and echo-challenge failures. Series appear only while strict KV-exact rules exist.

panels.title: KV event integrity & AI policy (KV-exact / API-key deployments)
KV event integrity
panels.description: Event-stream integrity for KV-exact routing. Wire rejects mean events were DISCARDED (stale inventory); reconnects risk gaps; watchdog trips mean sustained zero exact-hits while KV routing was active; drain faults are TRT-LLM destructive-read continuity violations (heals shown for comparison). Absent until a KV-exact deployment is active.

panels.title: P/D endpoint failures
panels.description: Prefill/decode endpoint failure handling: endpoints dying mid-stream, same-endpoint connect retries, and whether those retries succeed. Sustained retries without matching successes degrade P/D attach.

panels.title: Policy store / unmetered
panels.description: AI policy-plane health: requests handled while the policy store was unavailable (admission decisions degraded), and traffic completing without token metering (billing/quota undercount) by VIP.

panels.title: KV event staleness
panels.description: Age of the last ACCEPTED event batch per publisher (decoded + rank-verified; rejected payloads never count). A connected socket with steadily rising age is a publisher that silently stopped publishing - or an idle engine; read together with request traffic. Absent until a first batch is accepted.

panels.title: KV inventory freshness
panels.description: 1 while the per-endpoint KV inventory holds blocks from the current publisher incarnation; 0 after any clear (publisher restart, lossy gap, AllBlocksCleared) until the next stored block. fresh=0 with connected=1 means Tier-1.5 routing is running cold for that endpoint even though the socket looks healthy.

panels.title: P/D & KV inventory levels
panels.description: Point-in-time capacity state of KV-exact routing: per-endpoint inventory block counts, prefix-trie node count, and active P/D conversation sessions. A pinned-at-cap blocks count pairs with the eviction-pressure panel.

panels.title: KV inventory pressure
panels.description: Cap-eviction rate (publisher emitting BlockStored without matching BlockRemoved — the authoritative misbehaving-publisher signal) and Tier-1.5 cold-start seeds (bounded compensation diverting hits to cold prefill endpoints).

panels.title: P/D robustness events
panels.description: Backpressure and failover machinery: admission queueing/shedding, circuit-breaker flips and proactive heals, connect failovers, P/D-to-normal fallbacks, raw client shutdowns on selection failure, and llama.cpp admission-probe advisories.

panels.title: P/D stream terminations
panels.description: Abnormal stream endings on the P/D path: SGLang decode close-drains, oversize rejects, prefill aborts/reject relays, room retries, TRT context early exits, and zero-byte decode EOFs. Sustained nonzero here with healthy endpoints is an engine-side stream problem.

panels.title: Session & KV-param routing
panels.description: Conversation-affinity and KV-parameter extraction health per model: P/D vs normal session hits, KV params found vs missing on the request path, and full-proxy KV-param buffer overflows (params arriving past the buffered window).

panels.title: Full-proxy cache
panels.description: L7 full-proxy buffering state: total cached bytes, the largest single-connection buffer, and connections queued on cache pressure. bytes-series are byte-valued, conns queued is a count.

panels.title: Payload parser
panels.description: AI payload parsing health: call rate by protocol and outcome, p95 parse latency and p95 body size per protocol, and attribute-extraction rate. Latency series are seconds and body size is bytes; rates are per-second.
